---
title: "Week 3 · Bi-variate data. Correlation and causation"
subtitle: "Scatter plots, trend lines, the correlation coefficient and its pitfalls, and the first step towards cause and effect"
---

With two variables at once the questions change: how do they move together, how
strongly, and does one cause the other? The week builds the scatter plot from
scratch, introduces the correlation coefficient and its pitfalls, and closes
with the ideas the rest of the course rests on: cause, effect, potential
outcomes and ceteris paribus.

## What the deck covers

-   **Bi-variate data**, introduced with the Palmer penguins, and building a
    scatter plot step by step.
-   **The scatter plot**: what makes a scatter plot self-explaining (title and
    sources, axis labels and units, points, legends, a temporal dimension),
    shown with the height and weight of children under three from a nutrition
    study in Uganda.
-   **Trend lines** and examples of describing scatter plots; homework with
    further examples and drawing a linear trend line.
-   **The correlation coefficient**: methodology, interpretation, examples, the
    non-linearity pitfall and other pitfalls, the correlation matrix, homework
    and spurious correlations.
-   **Correlation and causation**: do we live longer because of a low birth
    rate? What it takes to establish a causal relationship; insights on the HIV
    pandemic from Gapminder.
-   **Example: rice yields and fertiliser application**: exploratory,
    univariate and descriptive analysis, the scatter plot, linearity and the
    linear transformation, correlation exam questions and the causality
    conclusion.
-   **Cause, effect, potential outcome and ceteris paribus**: cause and effect
    in rice yields, factual and counterfactual outcomes, treatment; randomised
    control trials, regression and innovation as three routes to ceteris
    paribus; an RCT example based on a nutrition education trial; potential
    exam questions.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Why this week has no interactive version

The scatter-plot section reads the SPSS file of the Uganda nutrition project
(`data-raw/uganda-poject/Uganda_B_E_agri and nutrition 04.06.2018.sav`), which
is not part of the public repository. The deck is therefore not in the render
list, and the PDFs above are the versions the students received. See the
[README](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/#readme) for how to
render it locally once the file is in place.
:::

## Data used

-   `penguins` from the palmerpenguins R package.
-   `UN11` (national statistics, including life expectancy and fertility) from
    the alr4 R package.
-   `RiceFarms` (Indonesian rice farms) from the plm R package, for the rice
    yield and fertiliser example.
-   The Uganda nutrition project survey, not published.
